extracted.intended_audience: publishers, preprint servers, scholarly-communications professionals, librarians, metadata managers, and researchers studying preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and improving the linkage between preprint records and their subsequently published journal articles by analysing metadata completeness, server practices, and publication outcomes (percentage linked, time-to-publication, destinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossref notification and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Crossref notifies preprint servers of potential matches with published articles. It requires preprint servers to verify the links and add them to the metadata record of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprint servers should act on Crossref-suggested matches by verifying and updating their preprint metadata to include links to the published article. The presentation notes that uptake of this requirement varies across preprint services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of links in preprint metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a preprint's metadata record includes a link to a published journal article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure as a binary flag per record or report the percentage of records with links. Absence of links can reflect metadata linking uptake rather than actual non-publication of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of preprints linked to journal articles (by server)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many preprints (as a percentage) have links to published journal articles, compared across different preprint servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare linkage percentages across servers and report server-level rates; useful to surface variability in metadata practices across providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The elapsed time between a preprint posting and the corresponding journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report distributions (median, mean, IQR) and compare time-to-publication across servers or disciplines to understand publication latency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination of preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals or publishers where preprints are ultimately published (the 'destination' of preprints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze where preprints end up to reveal publisher patterns and whether certain publishers/journals are more likely destinations for preprints from particular servers or disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences by preprint server type
rubrics_metrics.description: Variations in linkage rates, time-to-publication, and destinations between regional, disciplinary, and publisher-linked preprint servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify analyses by server type (regional vs disciplinary vs publisher-linked) to identify systematic differences in metadata linking and publication outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uptake of metadata linking
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall extent to which publishers and preprint servers adopt and implement linking practices in metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret observed linkage rates as reflecting both true publication rates and the degree of metadata uptake; low linkage may indicate the need for better metadata workflows rather than low publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset provenance and coverage (Crossref-collected COVID-19 preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a collection of COVID-19 related preprints from over 15 different preprint servers assembled via Crossref for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about dataset source and selection (here: Crossref-collected COVID-19 preprints across 15+ servers), since collection method affects coverage and generalisability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: availability of code and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Code and data for most figures are available on GitHub (link provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to analysis code and data to allow others to reproduce and inspect the analysis; this is presented as part of the work's good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action: include links in metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: A normative recommendation that publishers and preprint servers should include links between preprints and published articles in their metadata to improve the scholarly record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analysis results to advocate for better metadata practices: publishers and preprint servers should ensure links are present in metadata to aid discoverability and the integrity of the scholarly record.
